questions.title: Section A - Multiple Choice, Terminology, Matching, Meiosis/Mitosis, DNA and Protein Synthesis

subQuestions.questionText:
A gene is …
A) the complete set of chromosomes of an organism.
B) a segment on a chromosome, coding for a characteristic.
C) the haploid number of chromosomes in a cell.
D) a triplet of bases that codes for an amino acid.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2)
A gene is a segment on a chromosome that codes for a characteristic.

options.A: the complete set of chromosomes of an organism.
options.B: a segment on a chromosome, coding for a characteristic.
options.C: the haploid number of chromosomes in a cell.
options.D: a triplet of bases that codes for an amino acid.

subQuestions.questionText:
The significance of DNA replication is that the cells formed at the end of mitosis will …
A) be genetically identical.
B) contain half the number of chromosomes.
C) be genetically different.
D) have double the number of chromosomes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2)
DNA replication ensures the daughter cells formed at the end of mitosis are genetically identical to the parent cell.

options.B: contain half the number of chromosomes.
options.D: have double the number of chromosomes.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following statements is a feature of punctuated equilibrium?
A) Individual organisms adapt to changes in the environment.
B) The inheritance of acquired characteristics
C) There are long periods of little or no change in a population.
D) The more a structure is used, the more it develops.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2)
Punctuated equilibrium is characterised by long periods of little or no change in a population, interrupted by short bursts of rapid change.

options.A: Individual organisms adapt to changes in the environment.
options.C: There are long periods of little or no change in a population.
options.D: The more a structure is used, the more it develops.

subQuestions.questionText:
Haemophilia is …
A) characterised by the inability to distinguish between red and green.
B) caused by a mutation of an allele on the X-chromosome.
C) caused by non-disjunction of chromosomes during meiosis.
D) caused by an allele carried on an autosome.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2)
Haemophilia is caused by a mutation of a recessive allele on the X-chromosome.

options.A: characterised by the inability to distinguish between red and green.
options.B: caused by a mutation of an allele on the X-chromosome.
options.C: caused by non-disjunction of chromosomes during meiosis.
options.D: caused by an allele carried on an autosome.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is an example of a heterozygous genotype?
A) Xr Xr
B) BB
C) RW
D) aa
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2)
RW carries two different alleles, making it a heterozygous genotype (Xr Xr, BB and aa are all homozygous).

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents DNA replication, with molecules labelled 1, 4 and 5. Which ONE of the following combinations CORRECTLY identifies molecules 1, 4 and 5?
A) Molecule 1: Nucleotide; Molecule 4: Deoxyribose; Molecule 5: Phosphate
B) Molecule 1: Nitrogenous base; Molecule 4: Phosphate; Molecule 5: Deoxyribose
C) Molecule 1: Nucleotide; Molecule 4: Phosphate; Molecule 5: Deoxyribose
D) Molecule 1: Nitrogenous base; Molecule 4: Deoxyribose; Molecule 5: Phosphate
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2)
Molecule 1 = nucleotide, molecule 4 = deoxyribose (sugar) and molecule 5 = phosphate.

options.A: Molecule 1: Nucleotide; Molecule 4: Deoxyribose; Molecule 5: Phosphate
options.B: Molecule 1: Nitrogenous base; Molecule 4: Phosphate; Molecule 5: Deoxyribose
options.C: Molecule 1: Nucleotide; Molecule 4: Phosphate; Molecule 5: Deoxyribose
options.D: Molecule 1: Nitrogenous base; Molecule 4: Deoxyribose; Molecule 5: Phosphate

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents DNA replication, with molecules labelled 2 and 3. Which ONE of the following combinations is CORRECT for molecules 2 and 3?
A) Molecule 2: T; Molecule 3: A
B) Molecule 2: A; Molecule 3: A
C) Molecule 2: T; Molecule 3: G
D) Molecule 2: A; Molecule 3: C
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2)
Molecule 2 = A and molecule 3 = A, according to complementary base pairing on the replicating DNA strands.

subQuestions.questionText:
In a certain plant species, one gene controls stem colour and another controls plant height. The stem colour can be brown (B) or red (b), while the plant height can be tall (T) or short (t). Plant 1 is brown and short; Plant 2 is red and tall. When plant 1 was crossed with plant 2, some of their offspring were red and short.
Which ONE of the following represents the genotypes of plant 1 and plant 2?
A) Plant 1: bbtt; Plant 2: BbTt
B) Plant 1: Bbtt; Plant 2: bbTt
C) Plant 1: BbTt; Plant 2: bbtt
D) Plant 1: bbTt; Plant 2: Bbtt
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2)
Plant 1 (brown, short) = Bbtt and plant 2 (red, tall) = bbTt, which can produce red, short (bbtt) offspring.

subQuestions.questionText:
The number of possible different genotypes expected in the offspring from the cross of plant 1 (Bbtt) and plant 2 (bbTt) is …
A) 4.
B) 8.
C) 9.
D) 16.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2)
Bb x bb gives 2 genotypes and tt x Tt gives 2 genotypes, so 2 x 2 = 4 possible different genotypes in the offspring.

subQuestions.questionText:
A rare form of rickets is caused by a dominant allele on the X-chromosome. Which ONE of the following statements is TRUE about the inheritance of this form of rickets?
A) If the father is affected, all his sons will be affected.
B) It will be expressed more frequently in males than in females, since males have only one X-chromosome.
C) If the father is affected, all his daughters will be affected.
D) It will only be expressed in females, since they have two X-chromosomes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2)
For an X-linked dominant allele, an affected father passes his single X-chromosome (carrying the dominant allele) to all of his daughters, so all his daughters will be affected.

options.A: If the father is affected, all his sons will be affected.
options.B: It will be expressed more frequently in males than in females, since males have only one X-chromosome.
options.C: If the father is affected, all his daughters will be affected.
options.D: It will only be expressed in females, since they have two X-chromosomes.

subQuestions.questionText:

Description: The alleles of a gene separate into different gametes during meiosis.
A: Law of independent assortment
B: Law of segregation
subQuestions.memoText:
B only✓✓ (2)
The law of segregation states that the alleles of a gene separate into different gametes during meiosis.

- The remaining DNA bands are checked against the possible fathers'✓

- Stereoscopic vision✓

- Smaller jaws in humans✓ and larger jaws in African apes✓
- Small teeth/canines in humans✓ and large teeth/canines in African apes✓
- C-shaped palate in humans✓ and a U-shaped palate in African apes✓
- Humans are non-prognathous✓ and African apes are prognathous✓

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the significance of the position of the foramen magnum, the shape of the spine and the size of the pelvis in bipedalism.

- The spine is S-shaped✓ for better distribution of upper body weight✓/to absorb shock when walking upright/to allow flexibility

subQuestions.questionText:

subQuestions.questionText:
Starvation resistance refers to the period for which an organism can go without food before it dies. An investigation was conducted to determine the effect of the availability of food on the starvation resistance in fruit flies. The procedure was as follows:
- 5 000 fruit flies of the same age were used.
- They were all placed in a container suitable for the growth of fruit flies and were given a maltose-based food source.
- The food source was removed after an hour.
- The time it took for 80% of the fruit flies to die from starvation was recorded.
- The dead flies were removed from the container.
- The food source was then returned to the container.
- The remaining fruit flies were allowed to interbreed.
- Their eggs were collected and transferred to a new container with a food source where they were allowed to hatch.
- These fruit flies were allowed to grow to the same age as the 1st generation.
- The food source was then removed again.
- The time it took for 80% of the fruit flies to die from starvation was recorded again.
- This procedure was repeated until the 60th generation of fruit flies was reached.
State the independent variable for this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: Availability of food✓ (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how the dependent variable was measured.
subQuestions.memoText: They measured the time it took for 80% of the flies to die from starvation✓ (1)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE controlled variable that was considered when selecting the fruit flies at the beginning of the investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: Age✓ (Mark first ONE only) (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the investigator gave the fruit flies the same type of food throughout the investigation.
subQuestions.memoText:
- To improve the validity✓ of the investigation
- by ensuring that the availability of food is the only independent variable✓
- so that any changes that occur are only due to food availability✓
Any (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
The graphs in the question paper show the results obtained for the 1st generation (original population) and the 60th generation, plotting the number of flies against the hours until death from starvation. Describe the results obtained in this investigation.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
- The hours until death in the 1st generation was shorter✓/between 8 and 40✓ hours
- The hours until death in the 60th generation was longer✓/between 140 and 180✓ hours (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Using Darwin's theory of natural selection, explain the increase in starvation resistance in fruit flies.
subQuestions.memoText:
- There was variation in the population of fruit flies✓
- Some were starvation resistant while some were not starvation resistant✓
- When the food source was removed✓
- the fruit flies that were not starvation resistant died✓
- Those that were starvation resistant survived and reproduced✓ and
- passed on the allele for starvation resistance to their offspring✓
- The next generation had a higher proportion of fruit flies that were starvation resistant✓
Any (6)
